plan.title: bug(acceptance): no admitted acceptance-command form for JS workspace test runners (vitest) across scope:activate and verify:ac

narratives.Description: A web story whose tests run with vitest in web/ has no acceptance command that passes both scope:activate and verify:ac, because the two gates read different command records, the wrapper refusal hides the admitted forms and neither checks the working directory (#6882 item 3). This story gives scope:activate, xbrief:activate and verify:ac one non-executing record rule and record list, admits exactly `task <name>:test`, makes activation warn (never refuse) on records verify:ac would refuse, on cwd-grammar misses and on unpromoted captures, and adds one run-time real-path check in verify:ac as the only cwd enforcement.
narratives.Overview:
1. Record rule. `literal-acceptance/safety.ts` gains `evaluateAcceptanceCommandRecord({ command, cwd })`, returning the command verdict and a separate cwd verdict. The command goes through `evaluateCommandSafety` (with item 3 added). The cwd conforms when it is absent, empty or `.`, or when it is one or more segments joined by `/`, each matching `[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*` and none equal to `.` or `..`; anything else (absolute and rooted paths, drive forms such as `C:x` and `C:/x`, UNC and device paths, backslashes, `..`) is a cwd warning. The rule reads no file system, so every gate gives the same answer and the same reason text. A cwd warning never refuses, at activation or in `verify:ac`.
2. Run-time containment, the only cwd enforcement. Just before any runner call, `run.ts` resolves the real path of the project root and of `resolve(root, cwd)`. Both must succeed, and the second must be the root or inside it, compared with the platform's `path.relative` on the real paths (the result is not absolute and its first component is not `..`). A missing directory, a real-path error or an outside directory is `refused: <reason>` with exit 2, and no command is spawned. It covers every escape the grammar warns about, including `C:x`, an absolute path outside the root and a symlink that leaves the repository; an absolute path inside the root runs, with the item 1 warning. It does not protect against a directory replaced after the check.
3. One bounded wrapper shape. For first token `task` only, the command `task <name>:test` is admitted when `<name>` matches `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*` and nothing follows: no second task, no variable assignment, no flag. `deft` and `directive` are unchanged. `task web:test web:deploy`, `task web:test --dir x`, `task a:b:test` and `task web:deploy` are refused by the command rule. The existing `task test` form is unchanged.
4. One record list. `product-first-done-gate` gains `resolveAcceptanceCommandRecords(plan)`, which never runs a command. It reads records through the existing `resolveLiteralAcceptanceDetailed(plan, …)` with the options of the completion profile (`resolveAcceptanceGateProfile("complete")`), so inline prose mentions and operator "not a command" dispositions are moved to advisory exactly as `verify:ac` moves them, and prose-derived refusals stay advisory while structured refusals block. It adds the `plan.acceptance.commands` records that pass the existing `statedAcceptanceCommands` filter, each with source `explicit` and span `plan.acceptance.commands`. It applies item 1 to every record: a command refusal joins `blocking`, a cwd warning joins `cwdWarnings`. It also returns the unpromoted capture-only records, from the promotion check now inside `runLiteralAcceptanceCommands` (`run.ts` 156-217), moved into a non-executing function that both callers use unchanged.
5. `verify:ac` uses it. When `blocking` is not empty, `verify:ac` exits 2 before running anything and lists each refused record, as it does today for a structured refusal; this now includes a refused `plan.acceptance.commands` record. It prints `cwdWarnings` and goes on. It passes the resolved records to one `runLiteralAcceptanceCommands` call, whose existing promotion matching (unpromoted capture-only records fail before any run, as today) and execution-key grouping (each command, cwd and expected exit runs once, checked against every retained stdout expectation) decide what runs, and item 2 runs before each spawn. A filtered plan record is no longer skipped because a metadata record ran.
6. Both activation writers warn. `scope:activate` (`transition.ts`) and `xbrief:activate` (`vbrief-activate/activate.ts`, pending and already-active paths) call the resolver on every activation, whether or not the brief has acceptance-shaped narratives, and print one warning per record in `blocking`, `cwdWarnings` and the unpromoted list, each with `verify:ac`'s reason text and remedy (for an unpromoted record: promote the exact record into `plan.metadata.swarm.verify_commands`, or record the string in `plan.metadata.literal_acceptance_not_commands`). Activation does not refuse on any of them. The existing refusal in `evaluateAcceptanceActivateGate` (when acceptance-shaped narratives exist and `validatePlanAcceptance` fails) is unchanged, and the other narrative and clause rules are unchanged.
7. Declarations. The activation warnings and the `verify:ac` cwd warning are declared in `refusal-declarations/table.ts` in `warn` mode, print through the one helper with their gate id, and name the remedy `deft verify:ac --capture-only` on the brief, which lists each record and its reason. The item 2 run-time refusal is declared as `enforce` with the exception reason "an acceptance command must not be spawned outside the repository", and its CHANGELOG entry states that reason.
8. No persisted cwd refusal. Because the cwd grammar only warns and item 2 runs on every execution, no cwd refusal is written to the rejected ledger, so none can be dropped on reload. The rejected ledger and its reload recovery are unchanged.
9. One message. The wrapper refusal names the real list (`check|doctor|test|<name>:test (task only, nothing after)|verify:*|help|--version`) and the JS workspace form: `npx vitest run <path>` or `pnpm exec vitest run <path>` with `cwd: <workspace dir>`.
10. Docs and compatibility. `content/docs/plan-acceptance.md` gains an "Admitted command forms" section: the first tokens and their argument rules, the cwd grammar (a warning), the run-time check (a refusal), the JS workspace example (`{ "command": "npx vitest run src/app.test.ts", "cwd": "web" }`, or `task web:test`), that a capture-only record must be promoted before `verify:ac` runs it, that activation warns and does not refuse, and the claim in its narrow form: command-form admission and initial working-directory containment, under the assumption that repository test code is trusted; not isolation. The `types.ts` cwd doc changes. An absolute cwd outside the root is now refused at run time, stated in the CHANGELOG with the item 7 exception reason; the test at `literal-acceptance.test.ts` 645-655 is replaced by a refusal test, and the `cwd: sub` fixture at 216-225 creates its directory.
11. One PR. No new verb, flag, policy field or metadata key; the refusal table gains the item 7 rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a brief with `plan.acceptance.commands` `npx vitest run src/app.test.ts` and `cwd: web`, and a `web` directory, then `scope:activate` admits it with no warning and `verify:ac` runs it once with cwd `<root>/web`.
- Given the same record in both `plan.acceptance.commands` and `metadata.literal_acceptance_commands`, then `verify:ac` runs it once.
- Given a brief whose metadata holds one admitted command and whose `plan.acceptance.commands` holds a different admitted command, then `verify:ac` runs both.
- Given a `plan.acceptance.commands` record that is only an ingest copy of an inline prose mention, or that is listed in `literal_acceptance_not_commands`, then `verify:ac` runs nothing for it; given the same command with an independently promoted peer, then it runs once.
- Given a metadata-only capture-only record with no promoted peer, then `scope:activate` and `xbrief:activate` activate and print a warning with the promote-or-dispose remedy, and completion `verify:ac` refuses it before any run; given its promoted peer, then there is no warning and `verify:ac` runs it once.
- Given `task web:test` with no cwd, then `scope:activate`, `xbrief:activate` and `verify:ac` admit it with no warning.
- Given `task web:test web:deploy`, `task web:test --dir x`, `task a:b:test` or `task web:deploy` in `metadata.literal_acceptance_commands` on a brief with no acceptance-shaped narratives, then both activation verbs activate and warn with the item 9 message, and `verify:ac` exits 2 before running anything.
- Given a brief with acceptance-shaped narratives whose `plan.acceptance.commands` fails `validatePlanAcceptance`, then `scope:activate` refuses as it does today.
- Given a cwd of `../x`, `/x`, `C:x`, `C:/x`, `\\srv\share` or `web\sub`, then both activation verbs and `verify:ac` print the same cwd warning text and none of them refuses on the grammar.
- Given a cwd that resolves outside the project root (`../x`, `C:x`, an absolute path outside the root, or a symlink that leaves the root), or whose directory is missing, then `verify:ac` exits 2 with `refused:` and the runner is never called.
- Given an absolute cwd inside the project root, then `verify:ac` warns and runs the command there.
- Given a refused record only in `plan.acceptance.commands`, then `verify:ac` exits 2 and runs nothing.
- Given the refusal table, then the activation and cwd-grammar rows are in `warn` mode and the run-time containment row is `enforce` with the item 7 exception reason.
- Given `content/docs/plan-acceptance.md`, then the "Admitted command forms" section names the JS workspace example, the cwd grammar as a warning, the run-time check as a refusal, the promotion step and that activation warns, and says the rule is not isolation.
narratives.Constraint:
- Admitting `task <name>:test` by its first word with any tail, or bounding it with a namespace block list (comment 7049250343 finding 1).
- A cwd rule built on normalization plus a `..` prefix check, or a file-system check at activation (comment 7049250343 finding 2).
- One shared predicate over two different record readers, or letting a metadata record hide a `plan.acceptance.commands` record (comment 7049250343 finding 3).
- Any cwd verdict that can be dropped on reload; here no cwd refusal is persisted at all (comment 7049250343 finding 4).
- Checking only `scope:activate`, or an undeclared warning or refusal (comment 7049250343 finding 5).
- Describing the result as confining or isolating the process (comment 7049250343 finding 6).
- Adding plan records as executable without the existing inline and not-command exclusions, or a second deduplication beside the existing execution-key grouping (comment 7049403122 finding 1).
- Leaving activation silent about a record that completion `verify:ac` refuses before any run (comment 7049403122 finding 2).
- Reading the record list through `readStoredLiteralAcceptanceDetailed` alone, which skips the inline and "not a command" dispositions `resolveLiteralAcceptanceDetailed` applies.
- A new activation refusal in this release, or a refusal on the cwd grammar, against operator decision 7049854784.
- Any new first token, and any change to the title, sentence-floor or clause checks.

## In plain English
A consumer (#6882 item 3) could not find an acceptance command for a web story whose tests run with vitest in a `web/` workspace. `task web:test` is refused with a message that lists only `check|doctor|verify:*|help|--version`, so the author gave up and set `none_stated: true`. Reading the code at the pin: both places already call the same string check (`evaluateCommandSafety`), and `npx vitest run <path>` passes it. What differs is what each place reads. Activation checks only the command string of `plan.acceptance.commands`, and only when the brief has acceptance-shaped narratives. `verify:ac` also runs the stored metadata, swarm and plan-item commands. ## In plain English

The consumer needs a documented test command that activation accepts and verification actually runs in the intended workspace. The pinned code already admits `npx vitest run …`; the misleading message, different record readers, and unchecked working directory explain the inconsistency.

The shared-check approach is sound, but R1–R7 cannot bind unchanged. The wrapper needs a rule for its entire invocation, the directory checks need precise platform and filesystem behavior, and record resolution and rejection persistence need attention.

Answers to the seven questions:

1. **A closed wrapper form is possible.** A matching task name alone does not bound trailing tasks or flags. Blocking the `deft` namespace would not solve that.
2. **R1 is incomplete.** Windows path forms, filesystem failures, and the difference between activation checks and runtime checks need explicit treatment. Refusing absolute paths breaks an existing test.
3. **R2 does not yet establish one record contract.** Selection, normalization, rejection classification, and persistence remain separate.
4. **Both activation writers need the same command check**, including already-active revalidation.
5. **This introduces additional activation refusals**, even where it anticipates a later verification failure. The rollout needs to acknowledge that.
6. **The deferred argument issues can remain separate only with a limited safety claim:** directory containment is not process confinement.
7. **One PR remains reasonable**, with these corrections and the title/sentence-floor work still deferred.

All source citations below refer to dispatch commit `c9f0737c4e4778d86ab04981ee14298d4adfa38e`. Verification was by pinned source reads; no builds, tests, writes, or posts were performed.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Bound the entire new Task invocation

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/safety.ts:350–371` extracts the first subcommand and immediately accepts recognized names or prefixes. Its comment at lines 78–80 explicitly permits additional arguments. `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/run.ts:32–43` executes the complete original string through a shell with inherited environment.

**Failure mode:** Adding `<name>:test` to that acceptance branch also admits unchecked tails such as `task web:test web:deploy` or Taskfile/directory-selection flags. The first task name remains test-shaped while the invocation requests additional authority. The existing `task test` branch already has the corresponding weakness; that is not evidence that the new form is bounded.

**Disposition:** R3 needs an explicit whole-invocation grammar. The smallest addition is exactly `task <name>:test`, with no trailing tasks, assignments, or options. Any supported tail needs its own closed grammar. A namespace blacklist is insufficient.

A task wrapper can count under the existing trust assumption that repository test code is executable. Its name cannot prove what its body does. Dropping R3 is a viable smaller alternative because the direct Vitest form already exists; a completely bounded new wrapper form would make retaining R3 reasonable.

### 2. blocks-the-design — Separate lexical admission from runtime directory containment

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/run.ts:59–65,86–100` resolves `cwd` and passes it directly to the runner. `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/types.ts:37–41` explicitly permits absolute paths. `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/literal-acceptance.test.ts:645–655` asserts execution in an absolute temporary directory outside `projectRoot`.

**Failure mode:** “Normalize, then reject `../`” does not specify treatment of Windows backslashes, drive-relative `C:x`, rooted paths, UNC/device paths, or cross-drive resolution. “When the directory exists” also leaves missing directories and realpath failures unspecified. Separately, a filesystem-free activation check cannot reject an existing escaping symlink as R6 promises.

**Disposition:** R1 needs a portable relative-path grammar and component-aware containment comparison. Runtime must successfully resolve the root and an existing directory inside it immediately before invoking any runner; resolution failure must prevent execution. A directory created after activation gets checked at runtime. Windows case handling must follow platform path semantics, not a raw string-prefix comparison.

R6 should distinguish identical lexical refusals at both gates from filesystem-dependent refusals at execution, unless activation also performs filesystem checks. Absolute-path refusal is an intentional compatibility change requiring documentation and replacement of the cited test.

The existing containment machinery in `packages/core/src/fs/projection-containment.ts:41–50,58–145` provides useful patterns, but its write-target and missing-target semantics are not directly suitable for a runnable directory. Realpath checking also does not constitute protection against every concurrent filesystem replacement.

### 3. blocks-the-design — A shared predicate does not fix the different record readers

**Evidence:**

- `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/capture.ts:624–697` reads metadata, swarm fields, and items, but not `plan.acceptance.commands`.
- `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/evaluate.ts:69–79,88–120` supplies the existing blocking/advisory partition.
- `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:412–435` prefers resolved literal records over plan acceptance.
- The same file at lines 842–848 deliberately does not block on ordinary command-safety validation errors; lines 1073–1082 skip direct plan-acceptance execution once the literal path produced any run.

**Failure mode:** A plan can declare a workspace Vitest command while metadata contains a different executable command. Verification runs the metadata command and skips the plan command. Under R2, activation validates both independently, but verification still does not consume that same set. An unsafe plan-only record can likewise be rejected at activation while verification ignores its non-schema safety error and runs a safe metadata peer.

The parsers also differ: acceptance coercion preserves command text apart from trimming (`acceptance.ts:56–83`), while literal capture applies punctuation normalization (`capture.ts:41–59,719–787`).

**Disposition:** Both gates need a shared, non-executing command-record resolution and validation result, with explicit handling of divergent mirrors. Merging records or refusing conflicting mirrors are defensible choices; silently letting one store hide another is not. Reuse the existing advisory partition rather than reproducing it around `readStoredLiteralAcceptanceDetailed`. R6 needs plan-only, metadata-only, divergent-record, and different-`cwd` cases—not only identical copies in both fields.

### 4. blocks-the-design — Cwd refusals disappear from the persisted rejection ledger

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/capture.ts:123–127` removes rejected records from the accepted bucket. Lines 821–834 serialize accepted commands separately from rejections, whose stored fields contain no `cwd`. Lines 640–655 discard persisted rejections whenever the **command string alone** now passes safety. `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/types.ts:66–70` likewise defines no rejected-record directory.

**Failure mode:** With R1/R2, a record such as `{command: "pnpm test", cwd: "../outside"}` becomes a directory rejection. A subsequent attach operation can serialize only the remaining accepted records and its context-free rejection. On reload, the existing recovery check sees that `pnpm test` is allowed and drops the rejection. The failed acceptance requirement has vanished without being corrected.

**Disposition:** Record-level validation must extend through rejection persistence and recovery. Preserve sufficient record context, or retain authoritative invalid records and derive refusals from them. Command-only recovery must not clear a directory refusal. This can use the existing metadata key, but R7 must not prevent the necessary record-shape change. Add a reject → serialize → reload regression.

### 5. sharpens-framing — Cover both activation writers and declare the changed refusal behavior

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts:763–780` invokes the acceptance gate. `packages/core/src/vbrief-activate/activate.ts:161–207,244–267` instead uses lane/ingress checks on both already-active and pending paths. `packages/core/src/scope/lane-ingress-gate.ts:23–24` explicitly leaves the acceptance-activate gate outside that shared helper.

The current acceptance gate returns success without matching narratives (`acceptance-activate-gate.ts:73–80`). Thin briefs intentionally omit narratives (`intake/thin-brief.ts:149–167`). `main.md:97–100` requires warn-first rollout or a declared first-release enforcement exception for new refusals.

**Failure mode:** Changing only `scope:activate` leaves another route into active state unchecked. Conversely, indiscriminately moving all acceptance/schema checks outside the narrative condition could broaden unrelated requirements. A brief that previously activated can now be stopped even if it would later be cancelled without verification; absolute-directory refusal additionally rejects previously supported execution.

**Disposition:** Apply the shared **command** check to both activation writers, including revalidation, while preserving unrelated clause and narrative rules. Identify the new refusals and their rollout. Immediate enforcement for execution safety can use the existing named-exception mechanism; it should not be presented as behaviorally unchanged.

### 6. sharpens-framing — Describe containment narrowly enough to justify the deferred work

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/safety.ts:397–399,423–433,448–477` admits broad package-manager/test-runner argument tails. `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/run.ts:38–43` supplies a shell and inherited environment.

**Failure mode:** An inside-repository `cwd` does not prevent a runner from loading an outside configuration, selecting another root, accessing credentials, or executing arbitrary repository test code. Calling the resulting execution “confined to the repository” would overstate R1.

**Disposition:** The argument/fetch issues can remain follow-ups if the accepted claim is limited to **command-form admission and initial working-directory containment under trusted project-code assumptions**. If the intended guarantee is isolation from arbitrary effects or ambient credentials, this mechanism is insufficient and those deferrals cannot establish it.

What the critic found: the shared-check idea is right, but four parts were loose. A new `task <name>:test` form must be bounded as a whole command, not only by its first word. The working-directory rule must be a closed path grammar, with a separate file-system check just before a command runs. One shared check is not enough when the two gates read different records, so both gates need one shared record list. And a working-directory refusal must not disappear when a brief is saved and loaded again. It also asked that both activation verbs get the check, that the new refusal be declared, and that the safety claim stay narrow.

Solution this lean proposes: one closed record rule (command plus working directory) and one non-executing record list, used by `scope:activate`, `xbrief:activate` and `verify:ac`. The admitted forms for a JS workspace are `npx vitest run <path>` or `pnpm exec vitest run <path>` with `cwd: web`, and exactly `task web:test`. `verify:ac` checks again on disk just before it runs a command.

What this adds: one record rule, one resolver, one declared activation refusal, one doc section.

What it removes: the case where a brief activates and then `verify:ac` refuses a command the brief carried from the start, and the case where a plan command is never run because a metadata command hid it.

What it does not do:
- It does not isolate a command. A test runner still runs repository code with the inherited environment, and runner flags such as `--root` or `--config`, `npx` registry fetches, extra arguments after `task test`, and `run test*` script names are not narrowed.
- It does not change the title, sentence-floor or clause checks (#5856, #6218, #5861).
- It does not add a first token.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

What the critics found: the round-1 critic said the shared-check idea is right but four parts were loose: a new `task <name>:test` form must be bounded as a whole command; the working-directory rule must be a closed path grammar, with a separate file-system check just before a command runs; both gates need one shared record list, not only one shared check; and a working-directory refusal must survive a save and reload. The audit of the first lean held P1 and found two more gaps: adding plan records as plain executable records would make inline prose mentions and "not a command" captures run, and activation would still admit a capture-only record that `verify:ac` refuses until it is promoted.

Solution this lean proposes: one closed record rule (command plus working directory) and one non-executing record list, used by `scope:activate`, `xbrief:activate` and `verify:ac`. The list is read through the reader `verify:ac` already uses at completion, so inline mentions and "not a command" captures stay excluded, and plan records join it only through the filter `verify:ac` already applies to them. The admitted forms for a JS workspace are `npx vitest run <path>` or `pnpm exec vitest run <path>` with `cwd: web`, and exactly `task web:test`. Activation refuses what completion `verify:ac` would refuse before running anything: a refused command form or cwd, or a capture-only record that is not promoted. `verify:ac` checks again on disk just before it runs a command.

What this adds: one record rule, one resolver, one declared activation refusal, one doc section.

What it removes: the case where a brief activates and then `verify:ac` refuses, before running anything, a command the brief carried from the start, and the case where a plan command is never run because a metadata command ran.

What it does not do:
- It does not isolate a command. A test runner still runs repository code with the inherited environment, and runner flags such as `--root` or `--config`, `npx` registry fetches, extra arguments after `task test`, and `run test*` script names are not narrowed.
- It does not change the title, sentence-floor or clause checks (#5856, #6218, #5861).
- It does not add a first token.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

The command goes through `evaluateCommandSafety` (with item 3 added). The cwd conforms when it is absent, empty or `.`, or when it is one or more segments joined by `/`, each matching `[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*` and none equal to `.` or `..`; anything else (absolute and rooted paths, drive forms such as `C:x` and `C:/x`, UNC and device paths, backslashes, `..`) is a cwd warning. A missing directory, a real-path error or an outside directory is `refused: <reason>` with exit 2, and no command is spawned. It covers every escape the grammar warns about, including `C:x`, an absolute path outside the root and a symlink that leaves the repository; an absolute path inside the root runs, with the item 1 warning. It does not protect against a directory replaced after the check.
